title: IS Invoice Total Function
prompt: Write a function apply_discount(subtotal, rate=0.10) that returns round(subtotal * (1 - rate), 2).
hints: Compute subtotal * (1 - rate) and wrap with round(..., 2).
solution:
def apply_discount(subtotal, rate=0.10):
    return round(subtotal * (1 - rate), 2)
explanation: Default arguments let callers omit rate when the standard 10% discount applies.

title: Predict Local vs Global Scope
prompt: Type the exact two lines printed by the code.
hints: Assigning x = 99 inside test() creates a local variable.
The global x outside test() stays 10.
explanation: Assigning to a name inside def creates a local binding that does not overwrite the global variable.
code:
x = 10
def test():
    x = 99
    print(x)
test()
print(x)

title: Mutable default argument rule
prompt: Recall why mutable defaults are dangerous.
solution: Default values are evaluated once when def runs, so a mutable default is shared across calls.
explanation: Use None and initialize inside the function.
front: Why should you use `items=None` instead of `items=[]` as a default parameter?
back: Default values are evaluated once at function definition time, so `[]` would be shared and mutated across every call.
